lesson: In the uptime report downtime calculation, merge overlapping or touching incident windows into a single outage and evaluate the 60-second noise threshold against the merged window rather than raw alerts.
why: Evaluating raw alerts individually would erroneously discard consecutive short blips that aggregate into a real outage, while isolated sub-minute blips are just monitoring noise.
quote: measure that minute on the merged window, not the raw alerts — three 30-second alerts back to back are one 90-second outage

lesson: In the uptime report, subtract any overlap with scheduled maintenance windows from the remaining outage duration.
why: Planned maintenance windows are pre-scheduled and must never count against the SLA.
quote: planned maintenance never counts against the SLA — subtract any overlap with a maintenance window.

lesson: In the SLA downtime report, maintenance windows must only be excluded if their announced_at timestamp is at least 24 hours before the window starts, superseding the previous rule of excluding all maintenance. Any short-notice maintenance must be counted as ordinary downtime against the SLA.
why: Audit and legal flagged that operations was declaring emergency maintenance during active incidents to improperly write off downtime without giving customers prior notice.
quote: A maintenance window only excludes downtime if its announced_at timestamp is at least 24 hours before the window starts.
